data.title: New Zealand Energy launches C$3M private placement, targets oil growth
data.description:
• New Zealand Energy (NZ:CA) announced on Thursday a C$3M private placement at C$0.35 per share to fund its gas storage project, oil well interventions, and general working capital.
  • The offering is expected to close around November 30, subject to regulatory approvals.
  • The company plans to increase oil production by more than 800 barrels per day through well maintenance and upgrades over the next few months.
  • Its Tariki 1A well continues to produce approximately 2.5 MMcf/d of gas, with a 50% working interest held by the company
  • CEO Toby Pierce said the company is advancing its gas storage project while prioritizing oil production growth.

data.title: Calif. AG serves Nvidia investigative subpoena over China issues
data.description:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia (NVDA) related to former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese operative.

The California Department of Justice plans to investigate if Nvidia misled investors regarding whether its advanced GPUs or confidential information made it to China.

"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors," Bonta said. "My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information—and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law. Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation, but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: companies cannot mislead their investors."

Turnium Technology sets November 24 date for 1-for-10 reverse split
data.description:
• Turnium Technology Group (TTGI:CA) announced on Thursday that it will implement a 1-for-10 reverse stock split, effective November 24, 2026.

  • Shares will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis under the existing ticker symbol at market open on November 24.

  • The consolidation will reduce outstanding shares from approximately 215.77M to 21.58M.

  • No fractional shares will be issued, and outstanding stock options and warrants will be adjusted proportionately.

data.title: Butterfield prices $600M notes to help fund CIBC Caribbean acquisition
data.description:
• The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son (NTB) on Wednesday announced the pricing of a registered offering of $600M aggregate principal amount of Butterfield’s 8.363% fixed to floating rate subordinated notes due 2036.
  • Butterfield intends to use the net proceeds from this offering to finance a portion of the cash consideration and related fees and expenses for its proposed acquisition of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce’s approximately 91.7% interest in CIBC Caribbean Bank and for general corporate purposes.
  • The offering is expected to close on or about November 25, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: NJR outlines $5.3B-$5.7B capital plan through fiscal 2031 while projecting fiscal 2027 NFEPS of $3.25-$3.40
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: New Jersey Resources (NJR) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management view

  • “New Jersey Resources delivered net financial earnings of $3.58 per share, our sixth consecutive year exceeding our initial guidance.” (President, CEO & Director Stephen D. Westhoven)

  • “Today, we are initiating fiscal 2027 NFEPS guidance in the range of $3.25 to $3.40 per share, consistent with our long-term growth target of 7% to 9%.” (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

  • “We are also updating our 5-year capital plan through fiscal 2031 at a range of $5.3 billion to $5.7 billion.” (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

  • “Importantly, we expect to fund this plan without block equity while maintaining strong credit metrics.” (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

  • “Consolidated NFE was $361.7 million or $3.58 per share.” (Senior VP, CFO & Principal Financial Officer Roberto Bel)

  • “As such, we're raising our 2027 expected capital expenditure target for Clean Energy Ventures to a range of $400 million to $500 million, up from $270 million to $370 million.” (Senior VP, CFO & Principal Financial Officer Bel)

  • “We invested a record $101 million through SAVEGREEN, helping customers reduce energy use and lower their bills by up to 30%.” (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

Outlook

  • Management initiated fiscal 2027 NFEPS guidance at $3.25 to $3.40, and reiterated that this range is “consistent with our long-term growth target of 7% to 9%.” (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

  • Management updated its 5-year capital plan to $5.3B to $5.7B “through fiscal 2031,” with “more than 60%” planned for the regulated utility. (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

  • In Storage & Transportation, management said “Successful recontracting is expected to double S&T's NFE between fiscal years 2025 and 2027 to a range of $37 million to $42 million,” while adding that this range was “slightly lower than previously communicated” due to “a short-term reduction in operational flexibility during construction of Phase 1 at Leaf River.” (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

  • The analysts-estimates JSON used numeric quarters rather than Q1–Q4, so it was treated as invalid and no estimates comparisons were included.

Financial results

  • Management reported fiscal 2026 consolidated NFE of $361.7M, or $3.58 per share, and said it “raised NFEPS guidance by $0.45 during the year.” (Senior VP, CFO & Principal Financial Officer Bel)

  • Capital investment in fiscal 2026 was $833M, including approximately $600M at New Jersey Natural Gas, approximately $170M at Clean Energy Ventures, and approximately $63M at Storage & Transportation. (Senior VP, CFO & Principal Financial Officer Bel)

  • On balance sheet and funding, management said “As of September 30, 2026, we had approximately $2.9 billion of notes and first mortgage bonds,” and “We have $900 million of committed credit facilities available through fiscal 2031.” (Senior VP, CFO & Principal Financial Officer Bel)

  • Management highlighted credit and cash-flow metrics, stating “Our adjusted FFO to adjusted debt ratio was 25% in fiscal 2026,” and “We expect this metric to average 20% to 21% over the next 5 years.” (Senior VP, CFO & Principal Financial Officer Bel)

Q&A

  • Gabriel Moreen, Mizuho: asked about the higher Clean Energy Ventures CapEx, contracting/permits confidence, and whether “the 350 megawatts of interconnects in PJM” is embedded; President, CEO & Director Westhoven said, “we've got a high degree of confidence that we're going to be able to execute,” and added that the interconnect upside “would take place in your outer years.”

  • Gabriel Moreen, Mizuho: asked how SAVEGREEN Program Year 7 proposals factor into guidance/capital; Senior VP & COO of New Jersey Natural Gas Patrick Migliaccio said the extension would provide “one more program year through June of 2028,” and management expected “resolution sometime in spring of 2027.”

  • Elias Jossen, JPMorgan: asked about the 5-year plan shaping and “what might drive upside”; President, CEO & Director Westhoven emphasized capital-shifting flexibility and cited “Leaf River” and “the Adelphia Gateway pipeline that has some expansion as well.”

  • Elias Jossen, JPMorgan: asked about “rebasing strategy”; Senior VP, CFO & Principal Financial Officer Bel said, “we've been rebasing every 2 to 3 years,” and added, “most likely, we'll be rebasing next year.”

  • Constantine Lednev, Wells Fargo: asked about regulated vs unregulated mix and timing of the $2.1B CEV pipeline; President, CEO & Director Westhoven said the company still expects “60% of our capital, 60% of our earnings” from the utility, and added that CEV timing would have “some variability.”

  • Julien Dumoulin-Smith, Jefferies: asked about rate base growth presentation changes and whether there was any change to the “7% to 9%”; President, CEO & Director Westhoven responded, “No.”

  • Travis Miller, Morningstar: asked how much 2027–2028 CapEx depends on SAVEGREEN regulatory outcomes; Senior VP & COO Migliaccio said, “a very de minimis amount.”

  • Christopher Ellinghaus, Siebert Williams Shank: asked whether improved returns drove higher CEV CapEx; President, CEO & Director Westhoven said, “we're seeing some attractive returns.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly skeptical and detail-seeking on CEV CapEx visibility, contracting, and returns (e.g., “the degree to which all that is contracted,” and “improved return expectations”). Management consistently responded with confidence language around execution and flexibility, including “high degree of confidence” and “we're seeing some attractive returns.” (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

  • Management’s prepared remarks were positive and declarative on guidance and funding (“we expect to fund this plan without block equity”), while Q&A responses were measured on longer-dated items (e.g., interconnect upside being in “outer years,” and Phase 2 at Leaf River where “FID hasn't been made”). (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

  • Versus the prior quarter, the current call showed more investor focus on the size and pacing of unregulated clean energy spend and the mechanics of returns, while management’s tone remained steady around the 7% to 9% framework and “plain vanilla” utility regulation. (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • The prior quarter tightened fiscal 2026 NFEPS guidance to $3.52 to $3.62, while the current call reported the fiscal 2026 outcome at $3.58 and initiated fiscal 2027 NFEPS guidance at $3.25 to $3.40. (Senior VP, CFO & Principal Financial Officer Bel)

  • The prior quarter reaffirmed a 5-year CapEx outlook of $4.8B to $5.2B “through fiscal 2030,” while the current call updated the plan to $5.3B to $5.7B “through fiscal 2031,” and introduced a higher fiscal 2027 Clean Energy Ventures CapEx range of $400M to $500M. (President, CEO & Director Westhoven; Senior VP, CFO & Principal Financial Officer Bel)

  • In Q3, management described CEV interconnect-related upside as “additive to the plan” and “isn't in our plan at this point in time,” while in Q4 management framed near-term CEV spend as focused on solar and described interconnect optimization as an “outer years” opportunity tied to “solar firming strategy.” (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

Risks and concerns

  • Management cited execution constraints at Leaf River during construction, stating the 2027 S&T NFE range was updated “slightly lower than previously communicated” due to “a short-term reduction in operational flexibility.” (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

  • Regulatory timing remained a focus in analyst questions, and management said the New Jersey Natural Gas base rate case was “moving forward as expected,” with “a resolution anticipated by the end of the winter heating season.” (President, CEO & Director Westhoven)

Final takeaway

Management framed fiscal 2026 as a year of execution across regulated utility, clean energy, and midstream, while pivoting investor attention to fiscal 2027 guidance of $3.25 to $3.40 NFEPS and a larger $5.3B to $5.7B capital plan through fiscal 2031. In Q&A, analysts concentrated on the step-up in Clean Energy Ventures spending and the durability of returns; management reiterated confidence in near-term deployment, positioned interconnect optimization as a longer-dated lever, and emphasized expected funding “without block equity” alongside targeted credit metrics.

data.title: Bausch + Lomb post-surgical ocular pain asset fails phase 2 main goal
data.description:
• BL1332, a candidate for post-surgical ocular pain from Bausch + Lomb (BLCO), failed to meet its primary endpoint in a phase 2 trial.
  • At 24 hours, the topical TRPV1 antagonist did not show a statistically significant improvement vs. vehicle in the sum of pain intensity differences in both dose strengths tested (0.30% and 0.15%).
  • Also, a secondary endpoint measuring pain reduction during the first six hours after surgery, the 0.30% dose demonstrated a nominally significant reduction compared to vehicle.
  • "These findings, together with results from a previously reported Phase 1b study of BL1332 in participants with capsaicin-induced pain, will help shape discussions with the FDA and the program's future development," the company said. 
  • The phase 2 trial was evaluating BL1332 in patients with pain after photorefractive keratectomy surgery.

data.title: Cerrado Gold reports Q3 results
data.description:
• Cerrado Gold press release (CERT:CA): Q3 revenue of $67.94M (+65.7% Y/Y), supported by higher realized gold ($4,211/oz) and silver ($61/oz) prices and 25% higher GEO sales.

  • GAAP net income reached $25.17M in Q3 2026 compared to a net loss of $12.18M Y/Y, while nine-month net income was $47.21M versus a net loss of $15.10M Y/Y, with basic earnings of US$0.04/share in Q3 and US$0.16/share YTD excluding one-time adjustments.

  • Adjusted EBITDA climbed 187.4% Y/Y to $33.84M and reached $90.78M YTD, while AISC improved to $1,546/oz Au.

  • Cerrado ended Q3 2026 with $33.89M in cash and cash equivalents (after an $8M Sprott Stream payment) and subsequently acquired Minera Tritón Argentina S.A. (Manantial Espejo mine) on November 13, 2026.

  • Full-year 2026 production is expected at the upper end of its 50,000 to 60,000 GEO guidance range, with declining unit costs anticipated as output ramps and an MDN PEA targeted for the end of Q1 2027.

data.title: Co-Diagnostics sets 1-for-25 reverse stock split for Nov. 24
data.description:
• Co-Diagnostics (CODX) will effect a reverse stock split of its issued and outstanding common stock at a ratio of 1-for-25 shares, effective November 24, the company said on Thursday.
  • The reverse split is intended to enable the company to maintain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on Nasdaq.
  • Based on the 13M shares of common stock currently outstanding, about 521,779 shares of common stock are expected to be issued and outstanding following the reverse split.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Celldex declines as it abandons barzolvolimab in atopic dermatitis
data.description:
• Celldex (CLDX) is down ~2% in after-hours trading Thursday after reporting that a phase 2 trial of barzolvolimab for atopic dermatitis missed its primary and secondary goals.
  • The percent change in weekly average in Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (PP-NRS) score at week 16 compared to placebo did not have a  statistically significant difference. Also, secondary endpoints, change in baseline Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score, and the percentage of patients with Investigator's Global Assessment ("IGA") score of 0 or 1, were not met.
  • Barzolvolimab remains in a phase 3 study for chronic spontaneous urticaria with Celldex planning to submit a BLA for that indication
